The role will begin with a focus on defining methods and building robust systems to maintain and govern Supply Chain Master Data, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and usability across planning, execution, and reporting workflows. From there you will expand to strengthening the analytical foundations of supply chain planning—understanding how data flows across upstream and downstream processes, identifying where weaknesses enter the system, and designing scalable methods to detect, quantify, and reduce noise in planning inputs. You will combine statistical thinking with systems knowledge to distinguish real operational signals from data. Over time, this role is expected to expand into broader supply chain process optimization and decision science, including scenario analysis and stress-testing assumptions across areas such as inventory, sourcing, capacity, and network tradeoffs. You will have the opportunity to influence not just data, but the models and decision frameworks built on top of it. This is an end‑to‑end, hands‑on role for a data scientist who thrives in ambiguity, works closely with the business, and translates complex analysis into practical, implementable recommendations. You focus on what is most important, simplifying complexity without losing essential detail. You build trusting relationships through collaboration, clear communication, and openness to diverse perspectives. You adapt quickly in changing environments, stay curious, and continuously seek opportunities to improve systems, processes, and decision-making. You’ll contribute to this vital work while further developing your skills through our award-winning employee development programs.
